overall_quality.evidence: Processes and threads are both fundamental concepts in operating systems, but they serve different purposes and have distinct characteristics. Processes are the basic units of execution in an operating system, each with its own memory space and resources. Threads, on the other hand, are lightweight components within a process that share the same memory space and resources. Processes are used for running separate applications, while threads are used for performing tasks within a single application. Processes are more resource-intensive and have higher overhead, while threads are more efficient and can share data more easily.
